title: Sarga Three — verses 1–144
html:
Metre: upajāti (11 syllables per pada) and vaṁśastha (12 syllables) in alternation; verses 143–144 — praharṣiṇī.

Contents of the passage:
- 1–4 — Gauranga's youth; His teachers.
- 5–11 — the meeting with Lakshmipriya on the way to the Ganga.
- 12–24 — the match: Shachi keeps silent, Nimai reproaches His mother, Vanamali obtains her consent.
- 25–39 — Vanamali at the house of Vallabhacharya; the praise of the bridegroom; the consent of the bride's father.
- 40–49 — the preparations: the fixing of the date, the adhivasa, the nandimukha-shraddha, music and the cries of "ulu-ulu".
- 50–58 — Shachi, being a widow, cannot perform the rites; Nimai weeps for His father and consoles His mother.
- 59–62 — the bride is adorned; the procession with the palanquin to Vallabha's house.
- 63–70 — the wedding rite: the varana, the exchange of flowers and the first glance, the giving away of the bride, arghya and madhuparka.
- 71–74 — the return home; Shachi welcomes the newly-weds.
- 75–81 — married life; a description of Lakshmipriya's beauty (nakha-śikha, "from the toenails to the crown of the head").
- 82–95 — the journey to East Bengal: the people are enchanted by Him; the river Padmavati; He teaches there for several months.
- 96–101 — at home Lakshmipriya serves Shachi and pines for her husband; the snakebite.
- 102–105 — the physicians are powerless; on the bank of the Ganga she leaves her body.
- 106–118 — Shachi's lament over her daughter-in-law; the funeral rites.
- 119–125 — Nimai returns and consoles His mother: "She was not merely a human being."
- 126–144 — the second marriage: the matchmaking of Kashinatha, the consent of Sanatana Mishra, Vishnupriya; the adhivasa, the procession, the rite.

Verse 1

नवीनलावण्यसुधाम्बुधारा-
भृता नवीनेन सदङ्गकेन ।
तं यौवराज्ये सकलस्य यूनः
प्रसूनचापोऽभिषिषेच भूयः ॥१॥

navīna-lāvaṇya-sudhāmbu-dhārā-
bhṛtā navīnena sad-aṅgakena |
taṁ yauvarājye sakalasya yūnaḥ
prasūna-cāpo 'bhiṣiṣeca bhūyaḥ ||1||

navīna — of fresh; lāvaṇya — of loveliness; sudhā — of nectar; ambu — of the water; dhārā — with streams; bhṛtā — filled; navīnena — with youthful; sat — beautiful; aṅgakena — with the body; tam — Him; yauvarājye — to the rank of crown prince (to the kingdom of youth); sakalasya — of all; yūnaḥ — of young men; prasūna — of flowers; cāpaḥ — [he whose] bow [is]; abhiṣiṣeca — anointed; bhūyaḥ — again.

1With His youthful and beautiful body, filled with streams of the nectar-water of fresh loveliness, the god of the flower bow anointed Him once more as crown prince — sovereign of youth over all young men.

Note. "The god of the flower bow" is Kama, the god of love. A play on words: yauvarājya is "the rank of heir to the throne", but also "the kingdom of youth" (yuvan, a young man). The body full of streams of loveliness is itself, as it were, the vessel of the anointing.

Verse 2

पपाठ सत्पण्डितविष्णुनाम्नः
सुदर्शनादप्यतिहर्षभाजः ।
गुरुत्वमाकल्प्य महानुकम्पां
चकार हर्षादनयोः किमेषः ॥२॥

papāṭha sat-paṇḍita-viṣṇu-nāmnaḥ
sudarśanād apy ati-harṣa-bhājaḥ |
gurutvam ākalpya mahānukampāṁ
cakāra harṣād anayoḥ kim eṣaḥ ||2||

papāṭha — studied; sat — of the worthy; paṇḍita — of the pandita; viṣṇu — Vishnu; nāmnaḥ — by name; sudarśanāt — from Sudarshana; api — also; ati — of great; harṣa — joy; bhājaḥ — [from him] partaking; gurutvam — the position of teacher; ākalpya — having conferred; mahā — great; anukampām — kindness; cakāra — did; harṣāt — out of joy; anayoḥ — to these two; kim — was it not that; eṣaḥ — He.

2He studied under the worthy pandita named Vishnu and also under Sudarshana, who was filled with great joy. Was it not out of joy that He did these two a great kindness, granting them the position of His teachers?

Note. There are two teachers here, Vishnu and Sudarshana.

Verse 3

ततश्च वैयाकरणात्स गङ्गा-
दासादभूत्प्रत्यनुभूतविद्यः ।
यदेष विद्यामददाद्द्विजेभ्य-
स्तेनैव पुण्येन पपाठ सोऽत्र ॥३॥

tataś ca vaiyākaraṇāt sa gaṅgā-
dāsād abhūt pratyanubhūta-vidyaḥ |
yad eṣa vidyām adadād dvijebhyas
tenaiva puṇyena papāṭha so 'tra ||3||

tataḥ — then; ca — and; vaiyākaraṇāt — from the grammarian; saḥ — He; gaṅgādāsāt — from Gangadasa; abhūt — became; pratyanubhūta — [one by whom] was fully realized; vidyaḥ — learning; yat — because; eṣaḥ — that [teacher]; vidyām — knowledge; adadāt — used to give; dvijebhyaḥ — to the brahmanas; tena — by that; eva — very; puṇyena — by the merit; papāṭha — studied; saḥ — He; atra — here (with him).

3Then He mastered learning under the grammarian Gangadasa. Because that teacher used to give knowledge to the brahmanas, it was by that very merit [of his] that the Lord studied with him.

Note. Gangadasa Pandita was Nimai's principal teacher of grammar; all the biographies mention him.

Verse 4

सतीर्थवृन्दैः परिहासवद्भि-
र्हसन् विशेषं सवदावदेन ।
ततान लीलाप्रतिभानवार्त्ता-
मुर्वीसदुर्वीसुरवंशरत्नम् ॥४॥

satīrtha-vṛndaiḥ parihāsavadbhir
hasan viśeṣaṁ sa-vadāvadena |
tatāna līlā-pratibhāna-vārttām
urvī-sad-urvīsura-vaṁśa-ratnam ||4||

satīrtha — of fellow students; vṛndaiḥ — with throngs; parihāsavadbhiḥ — with jesting; hasan — laughing; viśeṣam — especially; sa — with; vadāvadena — eloquence; tatāna — spread; līlā — of playful; pratibhāna — wit; vārttām — talk; urvī — on the earth; sat — dwelling; urvīsura — of the brahmanas; vaṁśa — of the line; ratnam — the jewel.

4Laughing with throngs of jesting fellow students, and with especial eloquence, He — the jewel of the line of the brahmanas who dwell on the earth — spread talk full of playful wit.

Note. Urvī-sura, "god of the earth", is a brahmana (cf. kṣiti-deva, 2.9).

Verse 5

कदाचनासौ वनमालिनाम्नो
गृहे सदाचार्यवरस्य नाथः ।
जगाम सम्भाषरसेन हर्षा-
द्यदृच्छया श्रीमयगौरदेहः ॥५॥

kadācanāsau vanamāli-nāmno
gṛhe sad-ācārya-varasya nāthaḥ |
jagāma sambhāṣa-rasena harṣād
yadṛcchayā śrī-maya-gaura-dehaḥ ||5||

kadācana — once; asau — He; vanamāli — Vanamali; nāmnaḥ — by name; gṛhe — to the house; sat — of the worthy; ācārya — of the acharya; varasya — of the excellent; nāthaḥ — the Lord; jagāma — went; sambhāṣa — of conversation; rasena — for the relish; harṣāt — with joy; yadṛcchayā — by chance; śrī — beauty; maya — full of; gaura — golden; dehaḥ — [whose] body.

5Once the Lord, whose golden body was full of beauty, went by chance, joyfully, to the house of the worthy and excellent acharya named Vanamali, for the relish of conversation.

Verse 6

निवर्त्तमानेन ततः सुखेन
संभाष्य तं वर्त्मनि तेन तत्र ।
अकारि पीयूषमिव क्षरन्ती
नेत्रातिथिः काचनहेमवल्ली ॥६॥

nivartamānena tataḥ sukhena
saṁbhāṣya taṁ vartmani tena tatra |
akāri pīyūṣam iva kṣarantī
netrātithiḥ kācana hema-vallī ||6||

nivartamānena — by [Him] returning; tataḥ — then; sukhena — happily; saṁbhāṣya — having conversed; tam — with him; vartmani — on the road; tena — by Him; tatra — there; akāri — was made; pīyūṣam — nectar; iva — as if; kṣarantī — pouring forth; netra — of the eyes; atithiḥ — the guest; kā cana — a certain; hema — golden; vallī — creeper.

6Having conversed with him, He was returning happily, and there on the road He made a certain golden creeper, pouring forth nectar, as it were, the guest of His eyes.

Verse 7

सा वल्लभाचार्यसुता चलन्ती
स्नातुं सखीभिः सुरदीर्घिकायाम् ।
लक्ष्मीरनेनैव सहावतीर्णा
प्रभोर्ययौ लोचनवर्त्म तत्र ॥७॥

sā vallabhācārya-sutā calantī
snātuṁ sakhībhiḥ sura-dīrghikāyām |
lakṣmīr anenaiva sahāvatīrṇā
prabhor yayau locana-vartma tatra ||7||

sā — she; vallabha — of Vallabha; ācārya — of the acharya; sutā — the daughter; calantī — going; snātum — to bathe; sakhībhiḥ — with her friends; sura — of the gods; dīrghikāyām — in the pond; lakṣmīḥ — Lakshmi; anena — with Him; eva — indeed; saha — together; avatīrṇā — descended; prabhoḥ — of the Lord; yayau — came; locana — of the eyes; vartma — into the path; tatra — there.

7She was the daughter of Vallabhacharya — Lakshmi herself, who had descended together with Him. Going with her friends to bathe in the river of the gods, she there came into the path of the Lord's eyes.

Note. Sura-dīrghikā, "the pond of the gods", is the Ganga. This scene of the meeting by the river is found also in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 10.

Verse 8

विलोक्य स प्राक्तनवल्लभां तां
सुखाम्बुधौ मज्जनमाततान ।
नैसर्गिकं प्रेम यथावकाशं
प्रसह्य नामोदयतीह कं वा ॥८॥

vilokya sa prāktana-vallabhāṁ tāṁ
sukhāmbudhau majjanam ātatāna |
naisargikaṁ prema yathāvakāśaṁ
prasahya nāmodayatīha kaṁ vā ||8||

vilokya — having seen; saḥ — He; prāktana — of old; vallabhām — beloved; tām — her; sukha — of happiness; ambudhau — in the ocean; majjanam — immersion; ātatāna — performed; naisargikam — natural; prema — love; yathāvakāśam — as occasion offers; prasahya — forcibly; na — not; āmodayati — delights; iha — here; kam — whom; vā — indeed.

8Seeing her, His beloved of old, He plunged into the ocean of happiness. Whom indeed in this world does natural love not overpower with delight when the occasion offers?

Note. Prāktana, "former, of old": Lakshmipriya is the eternal consort of the Lord, Lakshmi.

Verse 9

तथाविधां तामवलोक्य रामां
मनस्यभूदुल्लसितः कृपाब्धिः ।
मणिं विना दुर्लभमाभिराम्यं
न हैमनी हारलता प्रयाति ॥९॥

tathā-vidhāṁ tām avalokya rāmāṁ
manasy abhūd ullasitaḥ kṛpābdhiḥ |
maṇiṁ vinā durlabham ābhirāmyaṁ
na haimanī hāra-latā prayāti ||9||

tathāvidhām — such; tām — her; avalokya — having seen; rāmām — lovely woman; manasi — in the heart; abhūt — became; ullasitaḥ — joyful; kṛpā — of mercy; abdhiḥ — the ocean; maṇim — a gem; vinā — without; durlabham — rare; ābhirāmyam — charm; na — not; haimanī — golden; hāra — of a necklace; latā — the strand; prayāti — attains.

9Seeing such a lovely woman, the ocean of mercy rejoiced in His heart. Without a gem, a golden necklace strand does not attain a rare charm.

Verse 10

सा शैशवादेकपदेन बाला
समागता यौवनसीम्नि किञ्चित् ।
परित्रुटच्चापलजायमान-
त्रपा तमालोक्य ननन्द शश्वत् ॥१०॥

sā śaiśavād eka-padena bālā
samāgatā yauvana-sīmni kiñcit |
parituṭac-cāpala-jāyamāna-
trapā tam ālokya nananda śaśvat ||10||

sā — she; śaiśavāt — from childhood; eka — with one; padena — with a step; bālā — the girl; samāgatā — having come; yauvana — of youth; sīmni — to the border; kiñcit — a little; paritruṭat — breaking off; cāpala — [whose] restlessness; jāyamāna — being born; trapā — [whose] shyness; tam — Him; ālokya — having seen; nananda — rejoiced; śaśvat — continually.

10The girl had come with a single step from childhood a little way over the border of youth: her childish restlessness was breaking off and shyness was being born. Seeing Him, she rejoiced continually.

Verse 11

अथाजगामैष निरीक्ष्य कान्तां
तैस्तैर्वयस्यैर्विहरंस्तथैव ।
पठन्सदोद्ग्राहपरः परेशो
रराज गूढस्थिररम्यलीलः ॥११॥

athājagāmaiṣa nirīkṣya kāntāṁ
tais tair vayasyair viharaṁs tathaiva |
paṭhan sadodgrāha-paraḥ pareśo
rarāja gūḍha-sthira-ramya-līlaḥ ||11||

atha — then; ājagāma — returned; eṣaḥ — He; nirīkṣya — having gazed at; kāntām — the beloved; taiḥ taiḥ — with those [same]; vayasyaiḥ — with friends; viharan — sporting; tathā eva — just as before; paṭhan — studying; sadā — always; udgrāha — on going over [lessons]; paraḥ — intent; pareśaḥ — the Supreme Lord; rarāja — shone; gūḍha — hidden; sthira — steady; ramya — charming; līlaḥ — [whose] play.

11Having gazed at His beloved, He returned, sporting just as before with those friends of His. Studying, ever intent on going over His lessons, the Supreme Lord shone, His charming play hidden and steady.

Verse 12

अथापरेद्युर्वनमालिनामा
प्रभोः य आचार्य उपेत्य वेश्म ।
नमश्चकार प्रणतो महात्मा
शचीं शुचिः संकथयन्विधिज्ञः ॥१२॥

athāparedyur vanamāli-nāmā
prabhoḥ ya ācārya upetya veśma |
namaś cakāra praṇato mahātmā
śacīṁ śuciḥ saṅkathayan vidhi-jñaḥ ||12||

atha — then; aparedyuḥ — on the next day; vanamāli — Vanamali; nāmā — by name; prabhoḥ — of the Lord; yaḥ — who; ācāryaḥ — the acharya; upetya — having come to; veśma — the house; namaḥ cakāra — paid homage; praṇataḥ — bowing down; mahātmā — the great soul; śacīm — to Shachi; śuciḥ — pure; saṅkathayan — conversing; vidhi — the proper rules; jñaḥ — knowing.

12Then on the next day the acharya named Vanamali — a great soul, pure and versed in the proper rules of conduct — came to the Lord's house, bowed low and paid homage to Shachi, and entered into conversation [with her].

Note. Vanamali Acharya acts as the matchmaker (ghaṭaka), as in the Chaitanya-bhagavata, Adi 10.

Verse 13

सुताय ते देवि वृतास्ति काचित्
कन्यातिधन्या गुणरूपशीलैः ।
सा वल्लभाचार्यसुता वराङ्गी
मूर्त्तेव लक्ष्मीः क्षितितोऽवतीर्णा ॥१३॥

sutāya te devi vṛtāsti kācit
kanyāti-dhanyā guṇa-rūpa-śīlaiḥ |
sā vallabhācārya-sutā varāṅgī
mūrteva lakṣmīḥ kṣitito 'vatīrṇā ||13||

sutāya — for the son; te — your; devi — O lady; vṛtā — chosen; asti — there is; kācit — a certain; kanyā — maiden; ati — very; dhanyā — blessed; guṇa — with qualities; rūpa — with beauty; śīlaiḥ — and with character; sā — she; vallabha — of Vallabha; ācārya — of the acharya; sutā — the daughter; varāṅgī — fair of form; mūrtā — embodied; iva — like; lakṣmīḥ — Lakshmi; kṣititaḥ — to the earth (?); avatīrṇā — descended.

13"O lady, for your son a certain maiden has been chosen, most blessed in qualities, beauty and character: that fair daughter of Vallabhacharya, like Lakshmi embodied, descended to the earth."

Note. Vṛtā ("chosen") can be understood in two ways: "chosen [as a bride] for your son", or "[the maiden] who has chosen your son". (?) Kṣititaḥ is an ablative ("from the earth"); the sense requires kṣitau ("on, to the earth"). The text is the same in Goswami's edition (GGM).

Verse 14

विधीयतां तत्र लघुप्रयत्न-
स्तनूजरत्नस्य विवाहकार्य्ये ।
यदीच्छसि श्रीमति तां सदङ्गां
श्रियं वधूरत्नमनिन्द्यशीलाम् ॥१४॥

vidhīyatāṁ tatra laghu-prayatnas
tanūja-ratnasya vivāha-kārye |
yadīcchasi śrīmati tāṁ sad-aṅgāṁ
śriyaṁ vadhū-ratnam anindya-śīlām ||14||

vidhīyatām — let be made; tatra — in that; laghu — slight; prayatnaḥ — effort; tanūja — of the son; ratnasya — of the jewel; vivāha — of the marriage; kārye — in the matter; yadi — if; icchasi — you desire; śrīmati — O glorious lady; tām — her; sat — beautiful; aṅgām — [whose] limbs; śriyam — Lakshmi; vadhū — of a bride; ratnam — a jewel; anindya — blameless; śīlām — [whose] character.

14"If you desire, O glorious lady, that Lakshmi of lovely limbs, a jewel of a bride of blameless character, then let but a slight effort be made in the matter of the marriage of your jewel of a son."

Verse 15

इत्यस्य संश्रुत्य वचोऽमृतं सा
तूष्णीमभून्नैव किमप्युवाच ।
अश्रद्दधाना वचनेऽस्य तस्मिन्
सुतेऽपि तल्लक्षणलक्षणार्था ॥१५॥

ity asya saṁśrutya vaco 'mṛtaṁ sā
tūṣṇīm abhūn naiva kim apy uvāca |
aśraddadhānā vacane 'sya tasmin
sute 'pi tal-lakṣaṇa-lakṣaṇārthā ||15||

iti — thus; asya — his; saṁśrutya — having heard; vacaḥ — the words; amṛtam — nectar; sā — she; tūṣṇīm — silent; abhūt — became; na eva — not at all; kim api — anything; uvāca — said; aśraddadhānā — not trusting; vacane — in the word; asya — his; tasmin — in that; sute — in the son; api — also; tat — of that; lakṣaṇa — the signs; lakṣaṇa — of noting; arthā — desirous.

15Having heard the nectar of his words, she fell silent and said nothing at all. She did not [fully] trust his word, and wished to note the signs of the same [desire] in her son as well.

Verse 16

नैवाकलय्याशु वचांसि शच्या
ययौ स आचार्यवरोऽतिदुःखी ।
विलोकयामास मनःकथाभिः
कषायितास्योऽथ महाप्रभुं तम् ॥१६॥

naivākalayyāśu vacāṁsi śacyā
yayau sa ācārya-varo 'ti-duḥkhī |
vilokayāmāsa manaḥ-kathābhiḥ
kaṣāyitāsyo 'tha mahāprabhuṁ tam ||16||

na eva — not at all; ākalayya — having heard; āśu — at once; vacāṁsi — words; śacyāḥ — of Shachi; yayau — went away; saḥ — that; ācārya — acharya; varaḥ — excellent; ati — very; duḥkhī — sad; vilokayāmāsa — saw; manaḥ — of the mind; kathābhiḥ — by the musings; kaṣāyita — clouded; āsyaḥ — [whose] face; atha — then; mahāprabhum — Mahaprabhu; tam — Him.

16Hearing no word at all from Shachi straight away, that excellent acharya went away very sad. Then, his face clouded by the musings of his mind, he saw Mahaprabhu.

Verse 17

असौ नवद्वीपकिशोरचन्द्र-
श्चन्द्राननश्चन्द्रसहस्रकान्तः ।
आचार्यमालोक्य ननाम हृष्टो
दृढं परिष्वज्य च धीरमूचे ॥१७॥

asau navadvīpa-kiśora-candraś
candrānanaś candra-sahasra-kāntaḥ |
ācāryam ālokya nanāma hṛṣṭo
dṛḍhaṁ pariṣvajya ca dhīram ūce ||17||

asau — He; navadvīpa — of Navadvipa; kiśora — young; candraḥ — moon; candra — moon-like; ānanaḥ — [whose] face; candra — of moons; sahasra — a thousand; kāntaḥ — lovely [as]; ācāryam — the acharya; ālokya — having seen; nanāma — bowed; hṛṣṭaḥ — joyful; dṛḍham — firmly; pariṣvajya — having embraced; ca — and; dhīram — calmly; ūce — spoke.

17He — the young moon of Navadvipa, moon-faced, lovely as a thousand moons — seeing the acharya, joyfully bowed to him, embraced him firmly and calmly said:

jāmātaraṁ vīkṣya samīpam āgataṁ
prodgamya harṣeṇa tanūruhaiḥ samam |
pādyāsanādyair varayāmbabhūva
kṣaṇena kanyāñ ca dadau sa kūkudaḥ ||141||

jāmātaram — the son-in-law; vīkṣya — seeing; samīpam — near; āgatam — arrived; prodgamya — having risen to meet; harṣeṇa — with joy; tanūruhaiḥ — with the hairs of the body; samam — together; pādya — with water for the feet; āsana — with a seat; ādyaiḥ — and the rest; varayāmbabhūva — chose [as bridegroom]; kṣaṇena — in a moment; kanyām — the daughter; ca — and; dadau — gave; saḥ — he; kūkudaḥ — the giver of the daughter.

141Seeing the son-in-law arrive near, he joyfully rose to meet Him — and the hairs of his body rose together with him; with water for the feet, a seat and the rest he performed the choosing of the bridegroom, and in a moment the giver of the bride gave away his daughter.

Note. Prodgamya is a play on words: Sanatana "rose" to meet the bridegroom, and his hairs "rose" from joy. The choosing of the bridegroom is the varaṇa. Kūkuda is a rare word: "one who gives an adorned daughter in marriage".

चक्रुः समानीय ततः स कन्यां
प्रादाद्द्विजस्तस्य पदाम्बुजेभ्यः ॥१४२॥

dvija-striyaḥ svastika-dhūpa-dīpair
amuṣya nirmañchanam ādareṇa |
cakruḥ samānīya tataḥ sa kanyāṁ
prādād dvijas tasya padāmbujebhyaḥ ||142||

dvija — of the brahmanas; striyaḥ — the wives; svastika — with svastika signs; dhūpa — with incense; dīpaiḥ — with lamps; amuṣya — for Him; nirmañchanam — the rite of protection; ādareṇa — with reverence; cakruḥ — performed; samānīya — having brought; tataḥ — then; saḥ — that; kanyām — daughter; prādāt — gave; dvijaḥ — brahmana; tasya — His; pada — of the feet; ambujebhyaḥ — to the lotuses.

142The wives of the brahmanas reverently performed for Him the rite of protection with svastika signs, incense and lamps; then the brahmana brought his daughter and gave her to His lotus feet.

Note. Nirmañchana is the rite in which lamps and incense are waved around the bridegroom to ward off the evil eye.

unmīlat-paṭu-paṭaha-prakṛṣṭa-ḍhakkā-

śrīmadbhir jaya-ninadaiḥ prasūna-vṛṣṭyā
rejāte smita-sumukhau parasparaṁ tau ||143||

unmīlat — breaking forth; paṭu — of clear-toned; paṭaha — of pataha drums; prakṛṣṭa — of mighty; ḍhakkā — of dhakka drums; nisvānaiḥ — with the roar; sphuṭa — with distinct; raṭitaiḥ — with the beating; ca — and; mardalānām — of mardalas; śrīmadbhiḥ — with splendid; jaya — of "Jaya!"; ninadaiḥ — with cries; prasūna — of flowers; vṛṣṭyā — with a rain; rejāte — shone; smita — smiling; sumukhau — [both] with lovely faces; parasparam — at each other; tau — the two.

143Amid the roar, breaking forth, of clear-toned pataha drums and mighty dhakkas, the distinct beating of the mardalas, splendid cries of "Jaya!" and a rain of flowers, the two shone, smiling at each other with lovely faces.

Note. The metre changes to praharṣiṇī (13 syllables) for the closing verses of the sarga. Pataha, dhakka and mardala are kinds of Bengali drums.
